pairs.why: A has fewer, larger checker squares and softer table edges, closer to the real card's low internal edge density, while B's tiny checkers add many fine edges.
A has soft, chunky, rounded edges with few internal lines, while B has thinner straps, small buckles and more fine seams, so it has higher edge density.
A's rim has a soft rolled edge and a diffuse shadow like the real clock, while B has a crisp flat silhouette with a hard ground shadow line.
B's smooth blobby contour and few crater edges match the real cards' low edge density, while A's faceted rock has many creases and edges.
Both tables have similar crisp small checkers and similar soft stone edges, so edges and linework give no reason to choose.
A has a simple silhouette with few internal edges, like the real pump, while B adds vents, cracks and extra panels that raise edge density.
A's hat has soft, rounded edges that melt into shading, while B has a razor-sharp brim rim and a hard black contour.
A has chunky simplified forms with few fine edges, while B's rods, grille slats and rail details add many thin hard edges.
